corso_laurea: MSc in Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Landscape
descrizione:
This course aims to provide students of Environmental Science and Technology with:
  • knowledge of the fundamental principles of hydrogeology and of the connection between groundwater and surface water as a single environmental system;
  • the ability to quantitatively study and analyse the main natural hydrogeological features and the human impact on them;
  • the ability to express complex scientific concepts clearly, both orally and in writing, with appropriate language and conceptual precision;
  • the ability to develop independent analysis and problem-solving skills for complex hydrogeological situations, in view of integrated water management.
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
  • quantitatively describe the geometric and hydrogeological structure of a complex environmental setting;
  • calculate the main hydrogeological parameters and understand their influence on the environment;
  • calculate groundwater flow velocity.
Judgement skills acquired:
  • analyse an environmental hydrogeological problem;
  • identify the most suitable tools for such analysis.
Learning skills:
  • apply the knowledge acquired to contexts different from those studied during the course;
  • understand scientific papers on the hydrogeological characterization of an environmental system.

docente: Prof: Tullia Bonomi, Giovanni Vezzoli, Monica Onida
corso_laurea: BSc in Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Landscape
descrizione:
This course aims to provide students of Environmental Science and Technology, approaching geological topics for the first time, with:
  • knowledge and understanding of the basic principles of the discipline, applied to the Earth's lithosphere and hydrosphere;
  • the ability to apply this knowledge and understanding to recognise and classify the main geological phenomena; to express complex scientific concepts in a simple way, with appropriate language and conceptual precision; and to learn directly through hands-on laboratory work on cartographic and petrographic topics. In particular, the cartography lab will give students the ability to read and use topographic maps and will teach the construction of some basic cartographic elements; the Petrography lab will give students the ability to distinguish between minerals and rocks, and to recognise and classify the main types of igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic rocks, relating them to their formation processes.
By the end of the course, students should have acquired:
  • the judgement skills needed to recognise and interpret the main geological phenomena linked to endogenous and exogenous processes;
  • the communication skills needed to describe the topics studied appropriately, using correct specialist terminology;
  • the learning skills needed to consult the relevant literature and independently integrate the knowledge acquired with that from other environmental science disciplines.

corso_laurea: BSc in Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Landscape
descrizione:
This course aims to provide students of Environmental Science and Technology with:
  • knowledge of the basic principles of 2D and 3D hydrogeological modeling approaches;
  • the ability to quantitatively study and analyse complex hydrogeological situations through hydrogeological and hydrochemical analysis;
  • the ability to develop a work project;
  • the ability to independently analyse situations and develop project proposals.
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
  • quantitatively model simple and complex hydrogeological structures;
  • reconstruct distributed maps from point data;
  • produce hydrogeological forecast scenarios.

By the end of the course, students will have acquired the judgement skills needed to analyse a complex environmental hydrogeological problem, carry out modeling work and write a technical report, just as they would in a real professional setting.

The course also develops learning skills, in particular the ability to apply the knowledge acquired to contexts different from those studied during the course, typical of the working world.

corso_laurea: MSc in Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Landscape
descrizione:
Knowledge and understanding. By the end of the course, students will:
  • know the key topics of Geology;
  • be able to draw logical connections between topics;
  • be able to identify the essential concepts and lines of reasoning.

Learning skills. By the end of the course, students will be able to consult the reference literature on the topics covered. They will also be able to independently design an educational/outreach lesson on key topics in Geology.

Judgement skills. By the end of the course, students will be able to assess the scientific accuracy of the information they wish to communicate, in particular by examining the sources used.

Communication skills. By the end of the course, students will be able to:

  • describe the topics studied appropriately, using correct specialist terminology;
  • use examples and metaphors to explain the more difficult concepts in the subject;
  • use new technologies to communicate topics in Geology clearly and effectively.

titolo: Laboratory for The Analysis of Freshwater and Groundwater
docente: Prof: Barbara Leoni, Veronica Nava, Marco Rotiroti
corso_laurea: BSc in Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Landscape
descrizione:
The main aim of this course is to provide students with:
  • knowledge and understanding of the main chemical, physical and ecological characteristics of surface and groundwater bodies, of surface–groundwater interaction processes, and of the main techniques used to monitor them;
  • the ability to apply this knowledge and understanding, specifically the ability to carry out the main fieldwork operations needed to monitor groundwater and surface water bodies, such as measuring flow rate and water/piezometric levels, laboratory analysis of selected chemical and biological parameters, and processing the data collected using computer tools;
  • judgement skills, enabling them to characterise surface and groundwater bodies and establish the type of interaction between them;
  • communication skills, in particular the ability to describe the topics studied appropriately using correct specialist terminology, and to structure a presentation of the results of field data collection, processing and interpretation;
  • learning skills, in particular the ability to independently integrate the knowledge acquired with that from other environmental science disciplines.

corso_laurea: MSc in Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Landscape
descrizione:
This course aims to provide students with:
  • knowledge and understanding
    • of the main categories of groundwater contaminants and their possible sources;
    • of the main processes governing contaminant movement in groundwater;
    • of the main groundwater remediation techniques and how they are implemented;
  • the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, specifically the ability to:
    • use the tools needed to assess the main natural and anthropogenic processes affecting groundwater quality;
    • develop a conceptual model of a contaminated site;
  • judgement skills, in particular:
    • the ability to assess human impacts on the groundwater environment and identify remediation measures;
    • the ability to solve problems related to groundwater contamination, from setting up a hydrogeochemical characterisation to choosing the most suitable remediation techniques;
  • communication skills, in particular the ability to:
    • describe the topics studied appropriately, using correct specialist terminology;
    • present the results of case studies drawn from scientific papers;
  • learning skills, in particular:
    • consulting the literature on the topics covered and independently integrating the knowledge acquired with that from other environmental science disciplines.
